//: A design record, not deployed state. No composite index is required today and
none is in the project — verified 31 Aug 2026 with
`gcloud firestore indexes composite list`, which returns nothing.
Firestore serves several equality filters from its automatic single-field
indexes. A composite index is only needed for equality combined with a range
or an order-by on another field, and the API deliberately has neither: it
filters on one or two equality fields and does the ordering and the rest of the
refinement in process over a bounded page.
These three are the places where that would stop being true. Move a sort or a
range into one of these queries and its index has to exist before the query

indexes.//: documents.find_by_hash: the upload cache. Two equality filters, so the automatic indexes serve it. Needs this only if it ever sorts or ranges.
sources.find_by_url: dedupes a watched address. Two equality filters, served automatically today.
alerts and the timeline. `list_alerts` reads an `in` filter with a limit and sorts in process precisely so this is not needed; ordering in Firestore instead would require it.
